8.text: I came across five deaf-mutes. Three of them were full-grown, and took

9.text: part in all the daily pursuits of their camp. They communicated with other

10.text: people by means of simple signs. Sleep, for instance, was expressed by leaning

11.text: the face on the palm; eating and drinking, by representative motions of the

12.text: hand to the mouth; woman, by forming an imaginary braid on each side of

13.text: the face; man, by pointing out the mustache; going, by a motion of two

14.text: fingers on the palm; etc. These signs are similar to those used by the Chuk-

15.text: chee for communicating with people who do not understand their language,

16.text: though no conventional signs exist in either case.

17.text: I met two dwarfs. One of them was married, and had three well-developed

18.text: children. There were several weak-minded people. One of them was a deaf-

19.text: mute; another had been struck with the palsy, and could not walk or move

20.text: his left hand. But the Chukchee had no notion of supernatural power possessed

21.text: by such people, as is held by the American Eskimo. Cases of violent madness

22.text: also occur. I was told by a woman shaman that she was out of her mind

23.text: for three years, because of a spell wrought on her by a rival. When in a

24.text: fit, she would lose all feeling in her wrists, and sometimes in her whole body.

25.text: At such times she would snatch a stone and pound her fingers with it, without

26.text: feeling any pain. In fact, the upper joints of two of her fingers were missing.

27.text: Frequently she would want to harm other people, and then her housemates

28.text: would tie her hands and bind her to one of the house-poles.

29.text: In another case I heard that a man of the Reindeer division of the tribe,

30.text: who for a long time was afflicted with similar fits, kept making attempts to

31.text: injure his camp-companions, and ultimately was put out of the way by common

33.text: Blindness occurs often, especially among old people. The young herdsmen

34.text: often have sore eyes on account of loss of sleep in the seasons when the

35.text: herding of the reindeer requires extra exertion, and because of the corrosive

36.text: action of sweat mixed with dirt. Snow-blindness in the spring is very common

37.text: among all who make journeys across the tundra. In treating inflamed eyes,

38.text: the lids are sometimes turned outward and bled by being rubbed with the

39.text: large hard larva of the reindeer-fly, the segments of which act like the teeth
